chunks: Ali, from his father, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Hammad, from Umar ibn Yazeed, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Inform me about the man who is absent from his family and commits adultery; is he stoned if he has a wife and he is absent from her?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The one absent from his family is not stoned, nor the slave who has not yet cohabited with his wife, nor the owner of temporary marriage (Mut'ah).' I said, 'So in which stage of his journey is he not considered married (Muhsan)?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'When he shortens (the prayer) and breaks (the fast), so he is not considered married.'

key_terms.الْغَائِبُ: The absentee, one who is away from his home or family
key_terms.مُحْصَنًا: Married/Chaste (a legal status entitling one to stoning for adultery)
key_terms.يُرْجَمُ: He is stoned (referring to the hadd punishment for married adulterers)

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for a traveling man to be considered married (Muhsan) for the purpose of stoning punishment in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi refines the juristic definition of 'Muhsan' by linking it to the practical application of travel concessions (qasr and iftar) rather than mere physical separation from one's wife. It highlights the Shia scholarly distinction that the heightened punishment of stoning applies only when the individual is fully integrated into the domestic sphere, excluding those in temporary marriage (mut'ah) or actively traveling. This criterion underscores the principle that legal status is often contingent upon ritual observance and lifestyle context.

en.hubeali: Ali, from his father, form Abdul Rahman Bin Hammad, from Umar Bin Yazeed who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘Inform me about the absentee from his wife, he commits adultery, would he be stoned when there was a wife for him and he was absent from her?’ Heasws said: ‘The absentee from his wife is not stoned, nor the slave who has yet to sleep with his wife, nor one with a temporary marriage’. I said, ‘So in which journey a Penalty (Hadd) would he not happen to be (classified as) a married man?’ Heasws said: ‘When he shortens (the Prayer) and breaks (the Fast), so he is not with the marriage’.
